title: Missing Values From One to N
statement:
You get an array nums of length n where every value lies between 1 and n. Some values appear more than once, so others do not appear at all.

Return every value in 1..n that is missing from nums, in ascending order. Try to do it with no extra memory beyond the output.

examples.why: n = 5. The values 1, 3 and 5 show up; 2 and 4 never do.
n = 2, and the repeated 1 pushed out the 2.
Every value from 1 to 4 is there, so nothing is missing.

gen: (r, big) => { const n = big ? 100000 : r.int(1, 10); return [r.arr(n, 1, n)]; }
hints: A set of the values you have seen solves it in O(n) time. Can the array itself play the role of that set?
Every value v points at an index, v − 1, that exists in the array. You can leave a mark at that index without losing the number stored there.
Mark index v − 1 by making the number there negative. Afterwards, every index i that still holds a positive number means i + 1 never appeared.

explain.intuition:
Because every value is between 1 and n, each value names a slot in the array itself: value v owns index v − 1. So the array can double as its own "seen" table. To mark a slot without destroying what is stored there, flip its sign. The size of the number is still readable with abs.

After one marking pass, a slot that is still positive was never named by any value. Its index plus one is a missing value, and reading slots left to right lists them in ascending order for free.
steps: For each value, read v = |nums[i]| (it may already be flipped) and make nums[v − 1] negative if it is not already.
Walk the array again. Every index i with nums[i] > 0 adds i + 1 to the answer.
Optionally flip all signs back so the caller gets its array unchanged.
pitfalls: Using nums[i] directly as an index after it was flipped negative. Always take the absolute value first.
Flipping with nums[v − 1] *= −1. A duplicate value flips it back to positive; set it to −|nums[v − 1]| instead.
Collecting the values that appear twice instead of the values that never appear. The output is about the empty slots.

solutions.title: Set of seen values
solutions.idea: Put every value in a set, then list the numbers from 1 to n that the set does not contain.

solutions.title: Mark slots by flipping signs
solutions.idea: Value v marks index v − 1 by making it negative. Positive slots at the end are the missing values.

followups: Return the values that appear twice instead, still with O(1) extra space.
The array is read-only. What is the best you can do on extra space now?
lcTitle: Find All Numbers Disappeared in an Array
